messages:
Diego (support L2): Heads up — Customer 'AcmeApps' opened an escalation: large p95/p99 latency spikes on their Dedicated pool in us-west-2 since ~14:05 UTC. They report requests taking multiple seconds and some timeouts. They say traffic is within their expected range (not a sudden huge burst).

Ashwin (eng-runtime): thx Diego. can you paste the exact model/route and sample request ids? also any request_id/timeouts from the API logs?

Diego (support L2): route: /v1/generate (model:redwood-large-llama-8q). sample request ids: req_8a1f..., req_8a2b... Customer included a span: p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~820ms, p99 to ~2.3s between 14:00-14:20. No deploy in their app.

Maria (sre): I pulled infra metrics for dedicated-usw2-a pool. Quick summary: CPU/GPU utilization hit ~96% and stayed there for ~18m. Autoscaler emitted decisions but new nodes didn't show Ready until ~10-12m after decision due to provisioning/backoff. That matches scale-up lag.

autoscale-bot: [14:09:07 UTC] scale_decision pool=dedicated-usw2-a current=4 desired=6 reason=queue_latency
autoscale-bot: [14:10:35 UTC] scale_attempt pool=dedicated-usw2-a attempt_id=at_102 prov_status=creating-instance
autoscale-bot: [14:18:40 UTC] scale_result pool=dedicated-usw2-a final_replicas=5 note=one-instance-failed-quota

Ashwin (eng-runtime): do we have any k8s/cni or cloud quota errors during that window? provisioning taking 10+ minutes is bad. Maria, can you paste the kube events and the first_failure logs?

Maria (sre): pasted logs below (trimmed):

```
kubelet: Warning FailedScheduling  "0/12 nodes are available: 4 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 8 node(s) had taints not tolerable..."
cloud-provisioner: ERROR provisioning: createInstance failed: quotaExceeded: "GPUs quota exceeded for account X"
autoscaler: scale_decision {"pool":"dedicated-usw2-a","current_replicas":4,"desired":6,"reason":"lagging_queue","time":"2026-02-18T14:09:07Z"}
```

Maria (sre): looks like cloud quota throttled one of the requested instances; second attempt was delayed by exponential backoff in our provisioner which added ~6m. Meanwhile the incoming workload caused backpressure and we fell back to spinning up a hosted variant which triggered cold GPU starts (OOMs/cold kvcache fills) for some requests — that explains the large p99s.

Nora (product): are customers routed to hosted automatically when Dedicated is saturated? we need to know fallback behavior (latency vs availability tradeoffs).

Ashwin (eng-runtime): yes, policy: when dedicated pool cannot serve within SLO we fallback to hosted-compatible variant of same model in region if available. Fallback saves availability but sometimes hurts tail latency due to cold starts / different hw. We should check whether fallback happened and how many requests hit hosted during the window.

Maria (sre): quick counts: 4.2k requests attempted on dedicated, ~380 requests were routed to hosted fallback between 14:08-14:20. Those had median latency 1.8s and p99 ~6.5s. That amplifies customer-facing p99.

Diego (support L2): Customer is unhappy because they expected dedicated capacity to avoid cold starts. They're asking for root cause and mitigation.

Ashwin (eng-runtime): immediate mitigation options (fast list):
- increase warm pool / minimum replicas for this customer's pool by +2 (manual bump)
- temporarily raise autoscale aggressiveness: lower cooldown and shorten backoff for provisioning retries (risky)
- disable fallback to hosted for this customer until pool stabilizes (risk outage)
- route them to a lower-latency model variant (smaller model) as an emergency mitigation

Maria (sre): I recommend manual pool expansion + enabling a faster provisioning path for critical pools (skip exponential backoff on second failure for account X) as short-term. For immediate customer relief I already raised desired_replicas to 7 via console — cloud is reporting 2 pending instances (on quota wait). Also opened a support ticket with cloud provider to lift GPU quota for the account.

SRE Oncall (pager): I'm going to execute a manual warmstart: pre-pull kv caches on one newly provisioned instance and bump the pool minReplicas to 5 to reduce future cold-start pain. Doing now.

autoscale-bot: action executed: set_min_replicas pool=dedicated-usw2-a min=5 by=SRE Oncall (pager) at 14:37 UTC

Ashwin (eng-runtime): followup items (medium-term):
- add explicit quota-health monitor and alert when cloud GPU quota is running low per-account/region
- change provisioner retry policy so a second parallel attempt can been started instead of waiting full backoff (limit to avoid runaway)
- instrument time-to-ready (provision->kube-ready) as a SLO metric and alert on >2m regressions
- better fallback heuristics: prefer local warm spare instances over hosted fallback for latency-sensitive customers

Diego (support L2): repro steps we shared with eng-runtime to validate locally:
1) generate sustained 400 rps for 10m against dedicated pool route (use load generator below)
2) temporarily lower minReplicas to 2 to emulate tight capacity
3) watch autoscaler logs and cloud provisioner events for quota failures

Load generator snippet:
```
# simple k6-like loop (pseudo)
for i in 1..400 do
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"lorem ipsum...","model":"redwood-large-llama-8q"}' &
end
```

Maria (sre): I added a short-lived alert: embargoed 'dedicated:pool_time_to_ready > 6m' to page infra and infra-sre if seen. Also filing an incident ticket to track root cause, remediation, and postmortem owners.

Nora (product): please include customer impact timeline and what we told the customer. we'll need a handoff to CS for follow-up and potential credit.

Diego (support L2): I told them: we identified provisioning + quota + fallback interactions causing spikes. We've raised pool min, requested a quota increase from provider, and will follow up with a timeline. They agreed to hold while we stabilize.

Ashwin (eng-runtime): final notes / todo owners:
- Maria: own incident ticket + kube/provisioner logs + cloud quota ticket (owner: Maria)
- Ashwin: prototyping a safer parallel retry path for provisioner and fallback policy change (owner: Ashwin)
- SRE Oncall: validate warmstart succeeded and confirm p99 returned to normal (owner: SRE Oncall)
- Diego: update customer and collect any additional request ids for auditing (owner: Diego)

SRE Oncall (pager): update: new instance became Ready at 14:45 UTC, pool at 6 replicas. p95 dropped back to ~210ms within 6 minutes of instance readiness. p99 still shows some tail from hosted fallbacks but trending down.

Diego (support L2): closing loop with customer with that update. They requested a postmortem and request for stronger guardrails to prevent fallback for dedicated customers — forwarding to product.

Nora (product): noted. we'll prioritize quota-health + fallback policy changes in the next sprint. also let's add a customer setting to control fallback behavior per-pool.

Maria (sre): I'll draft the incident postmortem and add the timeline + graphs (p95/p99) and remediation steps. Will share once ready. :thumbsup:
